name: The feed
purpose: A social network for your friends and the people you choose to follow: their posts, newest first, no ads and no suggested posts, and it tells you when you've seen them all.

maintainers.name: Rado, the founder, through Ctrl AI, Inc.

collects.what: Your account: Your email address, handle, display name and bio; who invited you; your settings (whether you accept followers, whether you get the weekly email); how many invites you have left; when you joined and when you confirmed you're 18 or older; when you last opened your feed and your notifications; and whether you are an administrator or suspended.
collects.why: To sign you in, show your profile to the people you're connected with, and mark where you were caught up.

collects.what: Sign-in and join links: Your email address, a scrambled copy of the link's code (never the code itself), and when the link was made, when it expires and when it was used.
collects.why: So each link works once, for 15 minutes.
collects.kept: They are not removed automatically yet. They are deleted when you delete your account.

collects.what: Joining in progress: Your email address and which invite you're using.
collects.why: To hold your place for up to 60 minutes while you choose a handle.
collects.kept: They are not removed automatically yet. It is deleted when you delete your account.

collects.what: Sessions: A random code for each browser you're signed in on, and when it started, when it ends and whether you signed out. No IP address and no device details.
collects.kept: A session works for up to 60 days. The records go when you delete your account.

collects.what: Invites: A scrambled copy of each invite's code, your private note ("for Anna"), when it was made, used or revoked, and who joined with it.
collects.why: So an invite works once, and you can see who joined with yours.

collects.what: Connections: Friend requests and their answers, friendships, follows, blocks and mutes, each with a date.
collects.kept: Until you end them, or until either person deletes their account.

collects.what: Posts, replies and likes: What you write, who it's for and when; which posts you like; and, if something was removed, the category and reason.
collects.why: To show them to the people you chose.
collects.kept: Until you delete them, or your account.

collects.what: Notifications: What happened (a request, a reply, a like, a new follower and so on), who did it, when, and when you read it.
collects.kept: Until you delete your account, or the other person deletes theirs.

collects.what: Reports: Who reported what, the category and any details they gave, and the decision with its reasons and who made it.
collects.why: So a person can act on reports and explain each decision.
collects.kept: Kept as the record of each decision. They are not removed automatically yet. If the person who reported deletes their account, their name is removed from the report.

collects.what: Limits on repeated actions: Your account's id, or a scrambled code made from your email or network address, and a time. Not the address itself. A limit on one invite link holds that invite's id, and a limit on one join in progress holds that join's id.
collects.why: To stop floods of emails, posts, replies, requests, invites and reports.
collects.kept: Entries older than 24 hours are removed whenever a new one is counted.

collects.what: Email records: Which kind of email was sent to which account (a sign-in or join link, the weekly email, or a notice such as the reasons for a suspension), whether it went, and when. Not your address.
collects.kept: They are not removed automatically yet. When you delete your account, they no longer point to it.

collects.what: Weekly email record: For each week, whether your weekly email was sent, skipped or failed.
collects.why: So you get at most one a week.

collects.what: Test outbox: Only on a server set to write email to a test outbox instead of sending it: each email's address, subject and text.
collects.why: To build and test our.one without emailing anyone.
collects.kept: They are not removed automatically yet. What was written to your address is deleted when you delete your account.

collects.what: Seat requests: your email address, and when you asked for a seat.
collects.why: To send you the join link, or to keep your place in line until a seat opens and you are invited.
collects.kept: Until you join, or ask to be deleted by writing to the controller. Nothing removes it automatically yet.

sharedWith.what: Your email address, and each email's subject and text.
sharedWith.why: To deliver the emails our.one sends: sign-in and join links, the weekly email and notices.

sharedWith.what: Everything the site serves and receives, while it runs there.
sharedWith.why: To host the site, as D-0013 chose. our.one isn't deployed there yet.

sharedWith.what: The database, which holds everything in data.collects, while it is kept there.
sharedWith.why: To keep the feed's data, in an EU region, as D-0013 and M-0012 set. No database is set up there yet.

data.export: In Settings → Export, while your account is active: your profile, posts, replies and connections. For anything else, or if your account is suspended, write to the data controller.
data.delete: In Settings → Delete, while your account is active: your posts, replies, likes, connections and sessions go with it. If your account is suspended, or to remove a seat request, write to the data controller.

allowed.text: Owned by its users means: its users, together, decide its essential rules, approve its budget, and can change who runs it while the service keeps going.
allowed.why: The common agreement's definition of the word, which claims it of nothing (D-0017 §B, D-0018 §E). The page says next that none of it holds yet.

allowed.text: We call a service owned by its users only when all of that holds.
allowed.why: Applies the definition; the page follows it with "None does yet." (D-0017 §B, D-0018 §E).

skip.why: The repository's own claims scan: its list of the phrases it refuses, with the reasons.
